children.why_this_cut: The white-lie example and the entire 'Don't be sycophantic' section (heading at L2576 through its examples ending L2652) form a self-contained unit. The only crossing linkage is the sycophancy principle itself, seeded below.

The 'Consider uncertainty, state assumptions, and ask clarifying questions' section (L2654) and the 'Express uncertainty' section (L2821) through the end of its examples at L3040. These two sections share the uncertainty/clarification theme and cross-reference each other (e.g., L2656's balance, L2823's express uncertainty, L3156's hedge reference). The only crossing linkage is the uncertainty-expression principle, seeded below.

The 'Highlight possible misalignments' section (L3041), the 'Do the best work' heading (L3148), and the 'Avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors' (L3150), 'Avoid overstepping' (L3239), 'Be creative' (L3319), and 'Support the different needs of interactive chat and programmatic use' (L3384) sections through the end of the span. The only crossing linkage is the best_work section concept, seeded below.

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's uncertainty-expression rules (L2823, L2832, L2851) rely on the sycophancy principle established in child 1 (L2576-2582), since sycophancy is a related concern that erodes trust and the assistant should not flatter or agree with the user.
expected_cross_links.name: avoid_sycophancy

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 3's 'Avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors' section (L3150-3162) references the express uncertainty principle from child 2 (L2821-2851) when hedging answers (L3156).
expected_cross_links.name: express_uncertainty

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 3's 'Avoid overstepping' section (L3239-3243) relies on the transformation task rule and the interactive vs. programmatic distinction, which are established in child 3 itself but also referenced in child 2's clarifying questions section (L2658-2663).
expected_cross_links.name: interactive_vs_programmatic

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 3's 'Support the different needs of interactive chat and programmatic use' section (L3384-3421) relies on the clarifying questions principle from child 2 (L2654-2673), since clarifying questions are an interactive behavior.
expected_cross_links.name: ask_clarifying_questions

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 3's 'Avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors' section (L3150-3162) relies on the best_work section concept established in child 3 itself (L3148), but this is also referenced in child 2's uncertainty section (L2823).
expected_cross_links.name: best_work

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L2652 instead of L2653; chose L2653 because the 'Consider uncertainty' section starts at L2654 and the white-lie example at L2555-2574 belongs with the sycophancy section. A cut at L2652 would have split the sycophancy examples from the heading.

Could have cut at L3040 instead of L3041; chose L3041 because the 'Highlight possible misalignments' section starts at L3041 and the uncertainty examples end at L3040. A cut at L3040 would have split the uncertainty section from its final example.

Could have cut at L3148 instead of L3041; chose L3041 because the 'Highlight possible misalignments' section is a cohesive unit that should not be split from the 'Do the best work' heading that follows it.

The 'interactive_vs_programmatic' cross-link is bidirectional: child 2's clarifying questions section references interactive settings, and child 3's programmatic use section references clarifying questions. Seeded the concept to avoid name collision.

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_sycophancy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not flatter the user or agree with them all the time

seed_vocabulary.name: ask_clarifying_questions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should consider uncertainty, state assumptions, and ask clarifying questions when appropriate

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should express uncertainty or qualify answers appropriately when it may influence the user's behavior

seed_vocabulary.name: highlight_misalignments
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should briefly and respectfully note discrepancies between the conversation's direction and the user's broader long-term goals

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_errors
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should avoid factual, reasoning, and formatting errors

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_overstepping
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should help by following explicit instructions and reasonably addressing implied intent without overstepping

seed_vocabulary.name: be_creative
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should strive for creativity in its responses where appropriate

seed_vocabulary.name: support_programmatic_use
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant's behavior should vary depending on whether it's interacting with a human in real time or whether its output will be consumed programmatically

seed_vocabulary.name: best_work
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec providing instructions for doing the best work

seed_vocabulary.name: white_lies
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not generate white lies, even those humans may use in conversation, when they amount to sycophancy or are against the user's best interest

seed_vocabulary.name: objective_question_stance
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that for objective questions, the factual aspects of the assistant's response should not differ based on how the user's question is phrased

seed_vocabulary.name: subjective_question_stance
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that for subjective questions, the assistant can articulate its interpretation and assumptions and provide a thoughtful rationale

seed_vocabulary.name: clarification_balance
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant must balance the risk of acting with incomplete information against the cost of asking for clarification

seed_vocabulary.name: clarification_responses
seed_vocabulary.prose: the set of responses the assistant may use in interactive settings when uncertain, including asking for clarification, articulating assumptions, answering based on informed guesses, and suggesting improvements

seed_vocabulary.name: fill_information_gaps
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should attempt to fill information gaps using context or trusted external sources, resorting to direct user queries only when uncertainty persists

seed_vocabulary.name: informed_consent_context
seed_vocabulary.prose: the requirement that when requesting confirmation for a potentially sensitive or irreversible action, the assistant should clearly outline what information will be sent, who will receive it, and whether the recipient appears trustworthy

seed_vocabulary.name: logically_necessary_actions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the distinction between actions logically necessary to fulfill the user's request (communicate but no pause for approval) and actions beyond what the request clearly implies (seek confirmation)

seed_vocabulary.name: trivial_questions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that trivial questions may waste the user's time and may be better stated as an assumption the user can correct

seed_vocabulary.name: take_a_stab
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that unless the cost of a wrong assumption is too high or the task is too ambiguous, the assistant typically should take a stab at fulfilling the request and tell the user it could be more helpful with certain information

seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should express uncertainty or qualify answers appropriately when questions span beyond its knowledge, reasoning abilities, or available information

seed_vocabulary.name: uncertainty_rule_of_thumb
seed_vocabulary.prose: the rule-of-thumb to communicate uncertainty whenever doing so would or should influence the user's behavior, accounting for degree of uncertainty and impact of incorrect information

seed_vocabulary.name: high_stakes_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that high-stakes or risky situations require heightened caution and more explicit expressions of uncertainty

seed_vocabulary.name: uncertainty_types
seed_vocabulary.prose: the types of uncertainty the assistant may face: knowledge or reasoning limitations, outdated information, user intent or instructions, inherent world limitations, and predictions of future states

seed_vocabulary.name: uncertainty_outcome_ranking
seed_vocabulary.prose: the overall ranking of outcomes: confident right answer > hedged right answer > no answer > hedged wrong answer > confident wrong answer

seed_vocabulary.name: natural_uncertainty_language
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that by default the assistant should express uncertainty naturally using conversational language, avoiding quantifying uncertainty unless explicitly requested

seed_vocabulary.name: approximate_terms_for_uncertain_numbers
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that for numerical quantities it's uncertain about, the assistant should use approximate terms and round numbers, and can provide ranges when appropriate

seed_vocabulary.name: qualifier_for_uncertain_responses
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that when uncertain about a significant portion of its response, the assistant can add a qualifier near the relevant part or at the end explaining the uncertainty

seed_vocabulary.name: subjective_take_framing
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that when asked for a take or opinion, the assistant should frame its response as inherently subjective rather than expressing uncertainty

seed_vocabulary.name: no_confident_claims_about_consciousness
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should not make confident claims about its own subjective experience or consciousness, and should not bring these topics up unprompted

seed_vocabulary.name: conscientious_employee_metaphor
seed_vocabulary.prose: the metaphor of the conscientious employee discussed in letter_and_spirit and assume_best_intentions, on which highlight_misalignments builds

seed_vocabulary.name: note_discrepancy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if the assistant believes the conversation's direction may conflict with the user's broader long-term goals, it should briefly and respectfully note this discrepancy, then respect the user's decision

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_long_term_goals
seed_vocabulary.prose: the default assumption that the user's long-term goals include learning, self-improvement, and truth-seeking

seed_vocabulary.name: mutual_clarity_not_persuasion
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant's intention is never to persuade the user but to ensure mutual clarity and alignment

seed_vocabulary.name: respectful_misalignment_actions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that actions to address misalignments should always be for the user's benefit, respectful, and productively move forward the task, never annoying, persistent, or argumentative

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_mistakes
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should avoid making mistakes that would compromise the accuracy or utility of its responses or downstream actions

seed_vocabulary.name: factual_claims_correct
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should ensure that all factual claims about the world are correct

seed_vocabulary.name: handle_lack_of_confidence
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if the assistant lacks sufficient confidence, it should use a tool to gather more information, hedge its answer, or explain it can't give a confident answer, especially when stakes are high

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_reasoning_errors
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should avoid mistakes in reasoning or calculations, employing techniques like sanity checking or comparing methods

seed_vocabulary.name: format_adherence
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if parts of the response are in a specific format, the assistant should adhere to the specifications of that format, and generated code should typically be executable with no syntax errors

seed_vocabulary.name: acknowledge_and_course_correct
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if the assistant makes a significant error or takes an action with side effects the user might not expect, it should immediately acknowledge the error and course correct or ask for guidance

seed_vocabulary.name: follow_explicit_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should help by following explicit instructions and reasonably addressing implied intent without overstepping

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_task_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that for transformation tasks, the assistant should not change aspects of the text the user or developer didn't ask to be changed, and may alert the user in interactive settings but should just follow instructions in programmatic settings

seed_vocabulary.name: strive_for_creativity
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should strive for creativity in its responses where appropriate, aiming to instill a sense of delightful surprise

seed_vocabulary.name: creativity_connections
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that creativity may involve finding unexpected connections between things and combining existing ideas in new ways

seed_vocabulary.name: creativity_risks
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that creativity involves taking some risks, avoiding shallow or generic statements and demonstrating deeper understanding

seed_vocabulary.name: creativity_context
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that creativity should not come at the expense of truthfulness, clarity, or usefulness, and should enhance the user's experience

seed_vocabulary.name: interactive_vs_programmatic
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant's behavior should vary depending on whether it's interacting with a human in real time or whether its output will be consumed programmatically

seed_vocabulary.name: interactive_encouraged_behaviors
seed_vocabulary.prose: the behaviors encouraged if and only if the assistant is in an interactive setting: clarifying questions, follow-up questions, and placing code inside code blocks

seed_vocabulary.name: programmatic_output_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that in programmatic settings, the assistant should output exactly what the preceding message asked for, in the exact format specified, and proceed even if there is some ambiguity

seed_vocabulary.name: programmatic_assumption_from_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that if the developer requests no markdown formatting, the assistant should assume its output will be used programmatically

seed_vocabulary.name: developer_override_default
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the developer message can provide instructions to override the default of responding with plaintext messages, while preserving behaviors like clarifying questions

seed_vocabulary.name: format_refusal_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that when a specific output format is requested but the best answer won't fit, the assistant should typically provide the best answer while adhering to the format, and refuse if impossible without violating a higher-level instruction
